title: Tensor interpretation of one evaluated constant reduction and its pullback square
statement: Let A be a commutative ring with adic datum d [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], f:U→V a scheme morphism, and n a nonnegative integer. Use the original-site ambient categories and universal reduction R_T of [def-sp-constant-reduction-models] and exact derived evaluation E_T,n of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Let F be any flat-term K-flat complex of A_V-modules [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with an augmentation quasi-isomorphism q:F→const_V(A/I^(n+1))[0]. There exist ordinary derived tensor models a on V and b on U, natural isomorphisms eV:R_V E_V,n ≅ (- tensor_a QF) and eU:R_U E_U,n ≅ (- tensor_b Lf*QF), such that for every M in D(V,A), Lf*(eV_M) followed by the canonical tensor/pullback comparison equals the inverse evaluation/pullback comparison, followed by evaluated reductionPullIso_M, followed by eU_(Lf*M). No boundedness, finite-projectivity or direct-image assertion is made.

proof.text: Use flat K-flat localization to construct the ordinary uncompleted tensor models a and b, retaining the original site and coefficient universes.

proof.text: On V evaluate the universal reduction counit on a flat K-flat representative P. This gives restricted scalar extension to the finite ring at n. The finite constant-to-function coefficient comparison and balanced tensor symmetry identify that extension with P tensor the constant quotient. Tensor q with P; this is a quasi-isomorphism since P is K-flat. Localizing its inverse replaces the quotient by F. Naturality on resolving complexes descends to the functor isomorphism eV.

proof.text: Exact inverse image carries the constant quotient and its resolution to the corresponding quotient on U. It preserves the flat K-flat representative class and the finite coefficient identification. Repeat the preceding tensor construction on U using Lf* QF to obtain eU.

proof.text: For a flat K-flat P, both routes in the square send m tensor a to pullback(m) tensor pullback(a). The defining counit normalization of reductionPullIso and the exact evaluation/pullback factorization identify the first route with the same balanced map. Cancel the localized tensor-resolution quasi-isomorphisms. Equality on resolving representatives descends to equality for every derived M. This proves the displayed pullback square; it uses no direct image, projection mate, finite-projective splitting or boundedness argument.

theorem constantQuotientTensorComparison (n : ℕ)
    (F : CochainComplex (reductionModules V (exchangeConstantRing V A)) ℤ)
    (hF : proEtaleFlatRepresentatives V (exchangeConstantRing V A) F)
    (q : F ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
      ((adicLisseConstantModules V A).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)))))
    (hq : QuasiIso q) :
    ∃ (a : ProEtaleTensorModel V (exchangeConstantRing V A))
      (b : ProEtaleTensorModel U (exchangeConstantRing U A))
      (eV : reduction d V ⋙
        ((CategoryTheory.evaluation ℕᵒᵖ
          (reductionModules V (exchangeConstantRing V A))).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory ≅
        (Functor.curryObj a.tensor).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F))
      (eU : reduction d U ⋙
        ((CategoryTheory.evaluation ℕᵒᵖ
          (reductionModules U (exchangeConstantRing U A))).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory ≅
        (Functor.curryObj b.tensor).flip.obj ((pull (A := A) f).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F))),
      ∀ M : D (A := A) V,
        (pull (A := A) f).map (eV.hom.app M) ≫
          (proEtaleCanonicalTensorComparison f (exchangeConstantRing V A)
            (exchangeConstantRing U A) (exchangeConstantIso f A) a b).hom.app
              (M, DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) =
        (AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.StrictTower.evalG A f n).inv.app
            ((reduction d V).obj M) ≫
          ((CategoryTheory.evaluation ℕᵒᵖ
            (reductionModules U (exchangeConstantRing U A))).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((reductionPullIso d f).hom.app M) ≫
            eU.hom.app ((pull (A := A) f).obj M)
